name: Ritz Classic
why_it_matters: Panjim's go-to Goan thali institution since 1978. The first-floor dining room on 18th June Road serves the city's benchmark fish thali — pomfret or mackerel curry, rice, sol kadhi, kismur — to a daily mix of office regulars and travellers chasing the real thing.
insider_tip: Get there by 12:30pm for the lunch thali — the fresh catch of the day sells out by 2pm and the queue on the staircase starts forming around 1pm. The mackerel rechad is the better order than prawns when monsoon prawns are small.
signature_address: Wagle Vision, 1st Floor, 18th June Road, Opposite Health Centre, Panjim, Goa 403001

name: Viva Panjim
why_it_matters: Run by Linda d'Souza out of her 150-year-old ancestral Fontainhas home on Rua 31 de Janeiro. A school-teacher turned cook, Linda dug up family-only Goan-Portuguese recipes — sorpotel, xacuti, ambot tik — that few other restaurants serve. State-government Lifetime Achievement award at the International Cuisine Conference.
insider_tip: The narrow alley seats only fill up after 8pm; book the indoor table near the kitchen for the cooler air. Skip dessert here and walk three minutes to Confeitaria 31 de Janeiro for bebinca instead — Linda's pork vindaloo is the headline order.
signature_address: House No. 178, Rua 31 de Janeiro, Behind Mary Immaculate High School, Fontainhas, Panjim, Goa 403001

name: Mum's Kitchen
why_it_matters: Founded in 1997 by Maria Suzette and Rony Martins as an 'Ethnic Cuisine Movement' to preserve Goan Catholic and Hindu home recipes that were disappearing. The Miramar bungalow lists each dish with the family it came from — sorpotel from one aunt, balchao from another. Outlook, Conde Nast and Lonely Planet have all run features.
insider_tip: Order the Goan tasting platter for two on a first visit — it's the only honest way to span four to five recheado/xacuti/cafreal styles. Reserve a garden-side table at lunch; the AC indoor room is darker and louder.
signature_address: House No. 854, Ground Floor, Martins Building, D. B. Marg, Miramar, Panjim, Goa 403001

name: Hospedaria Venite
why_it_matters: Open since 1954 inside a 200-year-old Fontainhas townhouse on Rua 31 de Janeiro. The wooden floors were salvaged from a Portuguese shipwreck; the tiny first-floor balcony tables that overhang the lane are the most photographed seats in Panjim's Latin Quarter. 'Hospedaria' means inn, and the upstairs rooms still operate.
insider_tip: There are only four real balcony tables — turn up at noon sharp or just after 7pm and ask specifically for 'balcony seating' or you'll be parked indoors. The pomfret rechad and a kingfisher beats the continental side of the menu.
signature_address: 31, Rua 31 de Janeiro, Near Head Post Office, Fontainhas, Panjim, Goa 403001

name: Confeitaria 31 de Janeiro
why_it_matters: Goa's oldest surviving bakery, opened on 31 January 1930 by Andre Mascarenhas after he returned from Bombay — the bakery and the street it sits on share the date. Still wood-fired, still preservative-free, still run by the Mascarenhas family (Gletta Mascarenhas leads the kitchen now). The bebinca and dodol are benchmarks travellers carry home in foil.
insider_tip: The shop is a counter-only takeaway, not a sit-down cafe — buy a slice of bebinca and a pao, walk two minutes uphill into the painted Fontainhas lanes, and eat them on a bench. Avoid the post-3pm lull when fresh bakes are between batches.
signature_address: S1, Rua 31 de Janeiro, Fontainhas, Panjim, Goa 403001

name: The Black Sheep Bistro
signature_dish: smoked pork belly with cashew feni glaze
why_it_matters: Husband-and-wife duo Prahlad and Sabreen Sukhtankar — both Les Roches Switzerland trained — opened Black Sheep Bistro in 2014 in a Portuguese-era mansion off Swami Vivekanand Road. It rewired Panjim's idea of a tasting-menu evening: local cashew feni in cocktails, Goan sausage in risotto, the Sukhtankars personally in the room.
insider_tip: Sit at the bar counter for the chef-driven experience and let Prahlad pair the feni cocktails — most travellers miss that the bar menu is more interesting than the wine list. Sunday afternoon is closed; reserve at least a day ahead in season (Nov-Feb).
signature_address: Swami Vivekanand Road, Next to ICICI Bank, Panjim, Goa 403001

name: Joseph Bar
why_it_matters: The standing-room corner bar that defines Fontainhas after dark. Originally a hyperlocal liquor shop run by Joseph Pereira selling feni, urrack and maad to neighbourhood regulars; nearly closed in 2017 before Atish Antonio Fernandes restored it. Today the Tambde Rosa cocktail (cashew feni, hibiscus, lime) is the signature pour and the spillover crowd onto 31 January Road is part of the show.
insider_tip: There is no sit-down dining — order a Tambde Rosa, take the plastic stool outside, and let the crowd happen around you. Cash-friendly, small UPI; arrive before 9pm or commit to a 30-minute wait on weekends.
signature_address: Rua 31 de Janeiro, Near São Tomé Chapel, Fontainhas, Panjim, Goa 403001
